sammendrag: The long-term effect of immigration will be determined by how descendants of immigrants fare. In this chapter, we use individual-level register data to compare the class position of descendants (aged 30–40) of immigrants from Pakistan, India, Morocco and Turkey with the population without immigrant background. Using a Bourdieusian class scheme, we contribute to the literature by studying class horizontally (cultural vs. economic capital) as well as vertically. We find that in the vertical class hierarchy, there are relatively small differences between employed descendants and the remaining population. This suggests that descendants are successfully integrated into the class structure. There are, however, clear horizontal class differences, as descendants are underrepresented in the cultural classes. This can partly be explained by descendants’ educational choices. We discuss possible reasons for this inequality and its implications.
tittel: Etterkommere av innvandrere i arbeidslivet – en bourdieusk klasseanalyse
